title: The Ramachandran plot
summary: Backbone dihedral angles φ and ψ are confined to a few sterically allowed regions, and secondary structures are those regions.

concepts.label: Protein structure
concepts.description: A PDB entry: atomic coordinates of a protein.

children.label: Residue
children.description: One amino acid in the chain.

children.label: Secondary structure
children.description: Helix, strand or loop, from PDBe.

children.label: Alpha helix
children.description: Residues near φ −63°, ψ −42°; i → i+4 hydrogen bonds.

children.label: Beta strand
children.description: Extended residues near φ −120°, ψ +130°, paired into sheets.

concepts.label: Ramachandran plot
concepts.description: The φ–ψ plane and its allowed regions.

facts.text: Ramachandran, Ramakrishnan and Sasisekharan derived the allowed regions from hard-sphere contacts in 1963.

children.label: Steric clash
children.description: Atoms closer than their van der Waals radii allow: what forbids most of the plane.

children.label: Structure validation
children.description: MolProbity's Favored / Allowed / Outlier verdict per residue.

concepts.label: Amino acid type
concepts.description: Glycine (no side chain) and proline (ring) have their own allowed regions.

concepts.label: Protein dynamics
concepts.description: Angles move in solution; NMR ensembles and MD show the spread a crystal hides.
